note: Each shape is the land that first appears in the Newberry atlas's states and territories on the dates of one acquisition (union of all versions valid on that date, minus the union the day before; slivers under ~500 km2 and boundary re-surveys narrower than ~2 km dropped). Claims (Oregon Country before 1846) and the independent Republic of Texas are not counted until they joined. Card facts: see each card's source.

items.title: Treaty of Paris
items.text: Britain recognised the independence of the United States in the Treaty of Paris, which ended the Revolutionary War. The new country reached from the Atlantic to the Mississippi, and from the Great Lakes to Spanish Florida.
items.source: Wikipedia, 'Treaty of Paris (1783)'; Newberry Library AHCB

items.title: The Louisiana Purchase
items.text: The United States bought Louisiana from France for $15 million, about 828,000 square miles (2.1 million km²). It nearly doubled the country. Its western limits were not clearly defined; France formally handed it over on 20 December 1803.

items.title: West Florida
items.text: The United States claimed the Gulf coast between the Mississippi and the Perdido rivers as part of Louisiana; Spain disagreed. US forces took possession of the part west of the Pearl River on 10 December 1810, and the rest was added to Mississippi Territory in 1812.
items.source: Wikipedia, 'Territorial evolution of the United States'; Newberry Library AHCB

items.title: The 49th parallel
items.text: The Treaty of 1818 with Britain fixed the border along the 49th parallel from the Lake of the Woods to the Rocky Mountains. The Red River basin south of the line became American.

items.title: Florida from Spain
items.text: In the Adams-Onís Treaty, signed on 22 February 1819, Spain ceded Florida and the two countries drew their first boundary across the continent to the Pacific. It took effect in 1821.

items.title: Texas joins
items.text: Texas had declared independence from Mexico in 1836. The United States annexed it by a joint resolution of Congress, and Texas became a state on 29 December 1845. Mexico had not recognised the loss, and war followed in 1846.

items.title: The Oregon Treaty
items.text: Britain and the United States had shared the Oregon Country since 1818. The Oregon Treaty of 15 June 1846 split it along the 49th parallel.

items.title: The Mexican Cession
items.text: The Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo, signed on 2 February 1848, ended the Mexican-American War. Mexico ceded about 529,000 square miles (1.4 million km²), today's California, Nevada and Utah and parts of four more states. The United States paid $15 million and took over $3.25 million of Mexican debts to American citizens.
items.source: Wikipedia, 'Mexican Cession' and 'Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo'; Newberry Library AHCB

items.title: The Gadsden Purchase
items.text: For $10 million the United States bought 29,640 square miles (77,000 km²) of southern Arizona and New Mexico, land suited to a southern railroad to the Pacific. It set today's border with Mexico.

items.title: Alaska from Russia
items.text: Russia sold Alaska to the United States for $7.2 million, adding 586,412 square miles (1.5 million km²), about two cents an acre.

items.title: Hawaii annexed
items.text: Five years after Queen Liliʻuokalani was overthrown, Congress annexed Hawaii by joint resolution, signed by President McKinley on 7 July 1898. The queen protested that her throne had been taken illegally.
